result.summary: Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC method for encrypting existing wallets, requiring nodes to be started with `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` to invoke it. Wallets can still be created with encryption enabled by passing a passphrase to `createwallet`. Documentation and functional tests are updated to create pre-encrypted wallets rather than encrypting unencrypted ones post-creation.
result.problem: Encrypting an existing unencrypted wallet exposes users to several hazards: new HD keys generated after encryption invalidate previous backups and can cause fund loss, residual unencrypted private key material cannot reliably be purged from disk or SSD flash storage, and encrypting wallets containing manually imported descriptors can silently alter spending conditions (#26607).
evidence: PR description: "No efforts are made to ensure that remnants of unencrypted key material are not left on the user's disk, as attempting to ensure this would be difficult and dangerous, and for some SSD's infeasible."

PR description: "Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user. (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26607)"
PR description: "Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds."
Tracks RFC issue #36027 ('Remove encrypting wallets that already exist').
result.scope_notes: The C++ change in src/wallet/rpc/encrypt.cpp is minimal (adding the rpcEnableDeprecated check); the bulk of the diff consists of mechanical functional test updates adapting tests to create pre-encrypted wallets.
result.card: Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC method for encrypting existing wallets, requiring the -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet configuration flag ahead of full removal in a future major release. Encrypting wallets upon creation via createwallet remains fully supported. Encrypting an already existing wallet is hazardous because generating new HD seeds post-encryption invalidates older backups (risking fund loss), residual unencrypted private key material remains on disk, and wallets with imported descriptors can have their spending conditions silently altered (issue #26607). The change unblocks issue #36027 to eliminate post-creation encryption. Most of the patch updates functional test suites to initialize pre-encrypted wallets.

risk.why: Deprecating an RPC interface can break downstream wallet automation scripts if they rely on encrypting existing wallets without setting -deprecatedrpc.
